kernels.l1: Adding is pressing the next button that many times.
kernels.l2: To add two numbers, start at the first one and press the next button as many times as the second number says. That is all addition is.
kernels.l3: Addition is defined by two rules: adding zero changes nothing, and adding the next of something is the next of adding it. Every sum unwinds to those rules, so 1 + 1 = 2 is something you derive.
kernels.l4: Addition is defined recursively: a + 0 = a and a + S(b) = S(a + b). Every sum unwinds to the base case, so 1 + 1 = 2 is a derivation rather than an assumption.
kernels.l5: The recursive definition determines addition completely; commutativity is not built in and must be proved by induction.
kernels.l6: Addition is defined by two rules: a + 0 = a, and adding a successor gives the successor of the sum. Commutativity and associativity are then theorems proved by induction rather than assumptions — which is genuinely surprising.
kernels.l7: a + 0 = a and a + S(b) = S(a + b) define addition recursively; every sum unwinds to the base case, and commutativity and associativity are theorems proved by induction, not axioms.
kernels.l8: Addition is defined by two rules recursing on the second slot, so one plus one becomes a derivation. That a plus b equals b plus a needs three inductions is the clearest sign that familiarity is not justification.
